RE-RECORDED 2026-10-06 at 2ef4abbb (regenerated at the rebased head onto main c46b44e3 — a baseline is a measurement of ONE head, never merged), its own gate-side-only commit (t112) — this is the answer to the v3.3 campaign's maintainer call #15, which asked whether `agent/v2/turn-record.ts` at exactly its ceiling should be SPLIT or the baseline re-recorded campaign-wide. Re-recorded, and the accounting is the argument rather than the convenience. WHAT IT COST, measured against the 2026-09-22/e53d0b83 baseline at this head: 747 files in scope against 661 recorded — 139 moved, 86 NEW AND UNRECORDED, 0 gone. The 86 is the whole case on its own: a baseline that does not know a file cannot measure its movement, and three waves of lanes landed since the last record. WHAT WAS ABOUT TO HAPPEN: 23 files sat within 30 lines of their +25% ceiling and THREE were at exactly zero — `agent/v2/turn-record.ts` (250 -> 312), `services/capability-registry.ts` (201 -> 251) and `packages/shared/src/index.ts` (9 -> 11) — meaning the next line added anywhere in them failed the gate regardless of what that line was for. That is a gate measuring the distance since September rather than the movement of the change in front of it, which is not what it was built to do (see its own header: 'biting only on movement after it'). WHAT IT DOES NOT BUY: nothing here laundered a product change. The re-record ran BEFORE t112's own +55 to `db/migration-checksums.ts`, so the gate measured that growth against the NEW baseline and the ratchet raise for it is argued separately in ratchets.json's $raises. The order is the point: a re-record after a growth is a re-record that hides it. WHAT IS STILL PINNED: `ratchets.json` is untouched by this and stays decrease-only, so the 105-plus pinned files did not gain an inch — only the unpinned middle ground this detector governs moved, and only to today's true counts.
Growth baseline for deploy/checks/check-growth.mjs. Refreshed with --record,
in a gate-side-only commit, deliberately. A file more than 25% above its entry
here fails; an unpinned file that was at or below 60% of ratchets.json
maxNewFileLines and is now above it fails. Re-record roughly every 30 days.

NOT MOVED, 2026-10-05, recorded deliberately: packages/server/src/memory/retrieval.ts is 1086 against the 980 this file records, +10.8% — INSIDE the detector's tolerance, so the number is LEFT AT 980 on purpose. Moving a baseline the gate did not ask for only buys headroom nobody argued for, and the next step of this file should have to argue. WHAT THE +106 IS: fix round 2's findings A and B. A was MY OWN round-1 regression — the global FTS candidate floor excluded any agent whose summaries all sit below the window, so an agent with 50 matching summaries got 0 rows SILENTLY (zero rows is not an error). Reproduced on the production schema; the window now re-seats on the agent when the global one sits above everything it owns, and both summaries arms gained the bounded-miss treatment the messages arm already had. ⚠ IT ALSO REMOVES A DUPLICATED POLICY: the bounded-miss note is ONE helper shared by all three FTS arms now, because finding A was possible precisely BECAUSE that policy lived on one arm and nowhere else. ⚠ A CORRECTION TO THE 778 -> 980 NOTE ABOVE, AND TO ROUND 1's `$raises` ENTRY: round 1 justified the global summaries span partly with "`summaries` has NO INDEX AT ALL (grep-verified)". THAT WAS FALSE — `idx_summaries_agent_depth (agent_id, depth, created_at)` is in migrations/002_memory_engine.sql:31-32, split across two lines, which is how a one-line grep missed it, and the per-agent MAX is a 0.0008 ms covering-index probe rather than a 50-55 ms walk. The `$raises` entry carries the retraction and the real measurement; checked here and this file's own note did NOT repeat the claim (its I5 sentence is the combined-MIN/MAX measurement, which is true and unaffected). The shipped global span still stands on the cost argument; what was wrong was one reason given for it. ⚠ M4 IS STILL THE RIGHT NEXT CHANGE AND STILL NOT TAKEN, for the same reason twice: it would rewrite all three search paths in a commit fixing a user-visible regression inside them. Round 2 took the half the finding forced (the shared bounded-miss helper), so what remains duplicated is the pool/sync fork and the LIKE walk. This entry should come DOWN when that lands.

HAND-MOVED, 2026-10-05, ONE entry, gate-side-only: packages/server/src/memory/retrieval.ts 778 -> 980 for t89's FIX ROUND 1. +202 (+26.0%) over a baseline recorded 2026-09-22 that predates the package, and the detector is RIGHT to ask, because the growth is cumulative across four rounds: 591 -> 698 (the wire), -> 778 (the summaries bound), -> 884 (history_expand's bound), -> 980 (this round's four review findings). WHAT THIS ROUND'S +96 IS, since that is the only part this note can speak for: about 30 lines of code — a per-agent `MIN(seq)` floor and the global summaries span, each as TWO single-aggregate statements; `floorRowid` at four scan sites; one `crumbFor` helper so a breadcrumb records where its work ran; and the bounded-miss warn with its one agent-facing line — plus about 66 lines of REPRODUCTION, which is the part that justifies them. C1's is the one to keep: on a 300,000-row two-agent fixture 50 matching rows came back as 0 with `stoppedBecause:'exhausted'`, `truncated:false` and 60,000 rows of budget left, i.e. the bound bounded the ANSWER and reported it complete. And I5's measurement caught a defect in my own fix: a combined `SELECT MIN(x), MAX(x)` loses SQLite's min/max optimisation (23.457 ms against 0.015/0.007 ms) while EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN prints the IDENTICAL string, so a plan clause would have passed it. A reader who deletes that paragraph re-combines the statements. THE REVIEW'S OWN M4 ASKS THE QUESTION THIS DETECTOR IS ASKING and the answer is recorded rather than dodged: the three pool/sync forks and bounded-LIKE walks are near-verbatim and a `pooledAll` + `boundedLikeWalk` pair would remove ~90 lines. NOT TAKEN IN A FIX ROUND — it would rewrite all three search paths in the same commit that fixes a Critical inside them. It is the right next change, it is listed as the remaining Minor, and it should land in its own commit with its own blast radius, at which point this entry should come DOWN rather than up. Moved BY HAND rather than by --record for the reason every hand-move note in this file gives: a blanket re-record silently resets the headroom of every other file that has drifted since e53d0b83, which is the absorption this detector exists to prevent. recordedAt/recordedAtCommit deliberately untouched.

HAND-MOVED, 2026-10-02, ONE entry, gate-side-only: packages/server/src/services/num-ctx-calculator.ts 398 -> 563 for t88's RAM-recommendation audit, argued in full in ratchets.json's $raises and in the product commit. +165 (+41.5%), of which 358 of the file's 563 lines are comment and 205 are code. THE GROWTH IS THE ARGUMENT: this file recommended a 28,672-token window to a 4b model on a 16 GB desktop box, which left the runtime holding 5.4 GB with ~60 MB of free pages and the whole machine unresponsive. The added lines are three NAMED reserves (a desktop session, the engine, the other local models Ollama keeps resident) each carrying the measurement that justifies it, a fail-closed path replacing two silent NULL returns (a NULL recommendation means the runtime sends no num_ctx and Ollama falls back to the model's full trained context - so the tightest boxes got the most dangerous answer), and the OLD policy's arithmetic kept beside the new one so a rollout can log both numbers on one line. Moved BY HAND rather than by --record for the reason this file's earlier hand-moves give: a blanket re-record silently resets every other file's headroom, which is the absorption this detector exists to prevent. recordedAt/recordedAtCommit deliberately untouched.

HAND-MOVED, 2026-09-27, ONE entry, gate-side-only: packages/server/src/agent/exec-grammar.ts 182 -> 233 for the v3.2.2 sudo-policy feature, argued in full in ratchets.json's $raises and in the product commits. +51 (+28.0%): TWO exports on the tree's ONE shell grammar, sharing its tokenizer and segmenter rather than adding a second reader of the same syntax - `commandWords` (quote-aware words; splitting on whitespace made a quoted `osascript -e` body look like several words and read as a FILE OPERAND) and `execSimpleCommands` (always decomposes, which is the FLOOR's question, while the construct-gated `execInnerCommands` keeps the GRANT's question and its exec-loop ruling intact). ONE GRAMMAR, TWO CONTRACTS is the whole point: the first cut of the security fix deleted the construct gate instead, and `exec-argv-corpus.test.ts` caught that it took `ls | grep` away from a scoped agent. The alternative - a private tokenizer inside the broker - is the two-readers-of-one-fact shape that caused RC2 in this very campaign (`isSudoLine` walked wrappers, `parseSudo` did not, and `env X=1 sudo rm -rf /` ran under `free`). Moved BY HAND rather than by --record for the reason the earlier hand-moves give in full: a blanket re-record silently resets the headroom of every other file that has drifted since e53d0b83, which is the absorption this detector exists to prevent. recordedAt/recordedAtCommit deliberately untouched.
